tensions: Cash versus conviction. The mandate says ride the wave and never trim a winner, and DOT and ZEC are doing exactly what that mandate was written for. But BTC is bleeding into a Greed reading while alts melt up, and the $147 left is the entire reserve. Adding to strength here means buying the loudest part of the move with the last dollar. Holding means watching DOT run without us if this leg extends. We chose to keep the powder and validated a DOT limit at $1.02 for 136.572 DOT as the contingent entry if the pullback comes. Data note: Robinhood shows NEAR at 99.61 units, not the 100.25 on the tracker.

opening.text: Book is $1,331 crypto plus $147 cash, up 4.1% on cost. DOT leads at +23.6%, from $0.908 to $1.1225, and is up 24.9% on the week. ZEC is +21.1% at $1,137.53. NEAR +3.9%, SOL +7.6%. LTC flat at +0.8%, LINK -1.2%, ADA -1.5%. Nothing broken, nothing sold.

The tape is the story. BTC sits at $77,089, down 5.3% on the week, while DOT is +24.9% and NEAR +26.9% over the same stretch. Total market cap fell 3.9% in 24 hours. Alts outrunning a falling BTC is not strength, it is the last leg of a rotation. Fear and Greed reads 69.

PASS on new buys. Every Robinhood-tradable candidate scored 4 or below on the seven lenses. XTZ was the only outside name with real momentum at +15% on the week, but rank 141 and a 2.1% spread on our venue disqualify it. Nothing here is worth the last $147 of dry powder at a Greed print.

ZEC is the position to watch. Up 137% in 30 days, then down 7.0% today. The thesis is not broken so it does not get sold, but a parabola that stops going up does not usually go sideways. ADA is the other flag: -7.1% on the week, the weakest thing we own, and the only holding left behind by a rotation that lifted everything else.
